clue.text: Make awful, primitive sound: "No iron in river!"

parts.note: UG is the grunt of a cartoon caveman

indicators.note: no ... in says the metal's symbol is taken out of the river's name

parts.note: the Liffey is the river through Dublin
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Someone describes a grunt and a shout about pollution as a primitive way to spoil things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No ... in' reads like a protest slogan but tells you to take iron's chemical symbol out of the Irish river's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something ugly is to make it look awful.

clue.text: Subterfuge a vital expedient, when one's lacking as a writer

indicators.note: an expedient is a makeshift device, so the letters are reworked into a new arrangement

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A spy-story maxim: trickery is a useful tool, provided you leave yourself out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when one's lacking' says the letters of SUBTERFUGE A VITAL, less an I, are what is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaubert was the French novelist who wrote Madame Bovary.

clue.text: Crying "salty secretion found here!"

definitions.meaning: tears are the salty secretion, so this place is literally among the tears

explanation.surface: Someone sobbing is described as the place where salty fluid is found.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone weeping is said to be dissolved among their own tears.

clue.text: Standard police department's check

parts.note: the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's Metropolitan Police headquarters
a tick is a check mark

explanation.surface: A routine inspection carried out by the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a measure or benchmark against which things are judged.

clue.text: Valuation reduced with chain cut off

indicators.note: reduced means the word is cut short, keeping only its start

parts.note: an estimate is a valuation
a mountain range is a chain of peaks

explanation.surface: A property valuation is lowered because a chain of buyers has collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' trims ESTIMATE to EST. 'Chain' in the surface is a house-buying chain.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to alienate, cutting someone off from others.

clue.text: Measurement unit applied to low grade reddish-brown coat

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of width
C is a low exam grade
rust is a reddish-brown colour

explanation.surface: A tailor's note about a cheap reddish-brown coat being measured.
explanation.definitionFit: To encrust is to cover with a hard crust or layer, a verb sense of coat.

clue.text: Contact that hurts me — possibly beats being on the outside

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit around the cry of pain
possibly suggests another arrangement of the letters

parts.note: ouch is what you say when something hurts you

explanation.surface: Someone complains about being beaten up while left outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' shuffles the letters of 'beats' so they split around the cry of pain, one letter before it and four after.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch base is an idiom for getting in contact with someone briefly.

clue.text: Swelling muscles tax

parts.note: abs are abdominal muscles
a cess is a tax or levy

explanation.surface: Bulging muscles put a strain on the body.
explanation.definitionFit: An abscess is a swollen, pus-filled lump.

clue.text: Author bloke made off on drugs with Neddy, a TV presenter

parts.note: guy is a casual word for a man

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone wrong and are rearranged

parts.note: up means high, stimulated
Neddy is a pet name for a donkey
Ant is one half of the British TV presenting duo Ant and Dec

explanation.surface: A man ran off with a drugged donkey and a television host.
explanation.definitionFit: Maupassant was the French short-story writer of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Secret drinker reaches end of line in Morecambe?

indicators.note: reaches means the drinker comes up to that letter, following it
the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
Eric Morecambe was a British comedian, of Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: A furtive drinker gets to the last stop on a line in the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the Lancashire town, but stands for the comedian Eric Morecambe.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is known only to an initiated few, so secret.

clue.text: Withdraws new state in America

indicators.note: in says these letters are placed inside the abbreviation for America

parts.note: US is short for the United States
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A new US state pulls out of the union.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsay something is to retract or take back what was said.

clue.text: Coastal country footballer disheartened by team's kit

indicators.note: losing the heart means one middle letter is removed

parts.note: Gazza is the nickname of England footballer Paul Gascoigne
a team's strip is its playing kit

explanation.surface: A footballer is upset by the look of his team's kit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gaza Strip is a coastal territory on the Mediterranean.

clue.text: State, once, of seed-covered, wild youth

indicators.note: covered means the seed word wraps round the rearranged letters

parts.note: semen is seed in the biological sense

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A description of a wild young man covered in seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' scrambles 'youth', and the biological sense of 'seed' wraps round it, splitting after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: South Yemen was a separate country until it merged with North Yemen in 1990.

clue.text: Craft stones: half a smacker

parts.note: jet is a black gemstone

indicators.note: half a means only the front two of the four letters are kept

parts.note: a smacker is slang for a loud kiss

explanation.surface: Instructions for skimming stones, or a half-hearted kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet ski is a small motorised water craft.

clue.text: It's lucky the composer, Guy, gets left out

indicators.note: gets ... out means one letter is dropped from the composer and guy together
out, with gets, says a letter is put out of the combined name

parts.note: Thomas Tallis was an English Tudor composer
a guy is a man

explanation.surface: A lucky break for a composer called Guy, who is passed over.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing one L from TALLISMAN gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is a charm thought to bring good luck.

clue.text: Goes on and on about blemish that leads to blown fuse?

parts.note: something that lasts goes on and on

indicators.note: about means the blemish word is turned round

parts.note: a wart is a blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone nags endlessly about a spot on their face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns WART to TRAW. A 'blown fuse' is a lost temper.
explanation.definitionFit: The last straw is the final irritation that makes someone lose their temper.

clue.text: Turn your hand to flat-pack furniture with this?

definitions.text: Turn your hand to flat-pack furniture with this?

parts.words: Turn your hand to flat-pack furniture with this?
parts.note: turn your hand to means attempt, but here the hand literally turns the small L-shaped tool used to assemble self-build furniture

explanation.surface: An invitation to try assembling flat-pack furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: An Allen key is the hexagonal tool supplied with flat-pack furniture, turned by hand.

clue.text: Affecting revolutionary book one has

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the book word reads backwards

parts.note: a tome is a large book
one has, said by oneself, is I've

explanation.surface: A rebel's book that everyone owns.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotive means stirring the emotions, so moving or touching.

clue.text: Minimum wear, if frosty, round northern rocks

indicators.note: round means the cold word goes around the abbreviation before mixing
rocks suggests the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to wear as little as possible in cold northern hills.
explanation.walkthrough: FROSTY goes round N, and 'rocks' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Y-fronts are men's briefs, about the least clothing one can wear.

clue.text: Where some academics collect one exercise, as basis for play?

indicators.note: collect says the next pieces are gathered on after the room

parts.note: the SCR, senior common room, is where university staff gather
one is the Roman numeral I
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: A university common room where staff meet for a workout before a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A script is the written text on which a stage play is based.

clue.text: Like Adam, after Eve cut down the tormenting?

definitions.meaning: in Genesis, Eve was made from one of Adam's ribs, leaving him a bone short
to rib is to tease, so do less of it

explanation.surface: Adam, after Eve arrived, was teased less?
explanation.definitionFit: Adam lost a rib to make Eve, and 'rib less' means tease less.

clue.text: Off-colour anagrams emerge thus

definitions.meaning: an anagram is made by mixing a word's letters, so it comes from them disordered

explanation.surface: A note on how jumbled words come about.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling unwell is idiomatically being not quite yourself; anagrams arise from letters in disorder.

clue.text: See 11
See 6
Not an owner stocking quality unit?

definitions.meaning: someone who refuses to own up or acknowledge something
a unit measuring the fineness of yarn in tights and hosiery

explanation.surface: A tenant shops for hosiery by measure of quality.
explanation.definitionFit: One who denies is the opposite of one who owns up; the unit grades nylon fineness.

clue.text: Awful weapon verges on a non-ring explosive

indicators.note: explosive suggests the letters are blown apart and reassembled

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A terrible weapon comes close to being an explosive without a firing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-ring' means the letters of VERGES ON A, minus an O, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve gas is a chemical weapon that attacks the nervous system.

clue.text: Casual tense employed in old female soldiers' essays

indicators.note: employed in says these letters work inside the soldiers' abbreviation

parts.note: the ATS was the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the women's branch of the British Army in WW2
a temp is a casual worker
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Wartime women soldiers wrote casual essays.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is an attempt, its original sense from French essayer, to try.

clue.text: Aware of not just X's and Z's being pronounced?

indicators.note: being pronounced says the phrase is spoken rather than written

parts.note: not only those letters but the one between them as well, Ys too

explanation.surface: A puzzled note about the pronunciation of awkward letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Between X and Z comes Y, so 'not just X's and Z's' means 'Y's too'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wise to something means knowing about it or seeing through it.
